metadata.title: Deion Burks - Taking over larger role
metadata.description: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday that Burks and Anthony Gould will step into larger roles after the team traded Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: A rookie seventh-round pick with 4.30 speed, Burks has caught six of nine targets for 60 yards across 49 routes (18.3 percent target rate, 1.22 yards per route). He won't necessarily see a lot of targets in an offense that runs through the RBs and TEs, but Burks should at least get far more playing time in the second half of the season, if only because the Colts' other wideouts are veterans with minimal history of production. Laquon Treadwell and Ashton Dulin are the other favorites for regular playing time, and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine is also on the roster.

metadata.title: Deion Burks to see expanded role
metadata.description: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Deion Burks will see an expanded role.
metadata.analysis: Burks has played a very limited role to begin the season. With the trades of Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, Burks is slated for an expanded role to finish the season alongside Laquon Treadwell.

metadata.title: Deion Burks - Notches one reception in Week 9
metadata.description: Burks played 17 of the Colts' 64 offensive snaps in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys, finishing with a zero-yard reception on his lone target.
metadata.analysis: A rookie seventh-round pick out of Oklahoma, Burks has seen sparse playing time through the Colts' first nine games. He's logged less than one-third of the snaps in each of those contests and has posted a 6-60-0 receiving line on nine targets go with 21 yards on three carries. Despite his modest output to date, Burks could nonetheless be primed for more opportunities in the Indianapolis passing game over the second half of the season. Tight end Tyler Warren will likely rank as the team's top pass-catching option, but the Colts should have plenty of targets left over after trading away Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday. Meanwhile, top wideout Alec Pierce (heel) lacks a clear timeline to return from injured reserve.

metadata.title: Deion Burks a Deep-League Waiver Wire Stash Following Colts' Trades
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts rookie wide receiver Deion Burks has played a limited role in his team's offense so far this season, recording six catches for 60 yards on nine targets across nine games. However, Burks could get his opportunity to prove himself in Indianapolis down the stretch. The Colts traded away two veteran wideouts at Tuesday's trade deadline, sending Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers and Josh Downs to the Kansas City Chiefs. With WR1 Alec Pierce (heel) on Injured Reserve and not expected to return in the near future, Indianapolis has very few proven pass-catchers outside of tight end Tyler Warren. While Burks is not guaranteed to see an increase in targets, he's a higher-upside option for deep-league fantasy managers than veteran Colts wide receivers Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.

metadata.title: Deion Burks goes for 41 yards in loss to Titans
metadata.description: Deion Burks caught both of his targets for 41 yards in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday. He also ran once for seven yards.
metadata.analysis: The rookie had only caught one of four targets on the season leading into Sunday, but he put up a nice splash play for 36 yards. He could work his way into a larger workload if the Colts find his ability as a deep threat is superior to that of Laquon Treadwell.

metadata.title: Deion Burks - Picked by Colts
metadata.description: The Colts selected Burks in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft, 254th overall.
metadata.analysis: No one would have thought anything of it if the Colts had taken Burks in the fourth round rather than the seventh, so this can only be seen as a close to the ideal end-of-draft selection. Burks' lack of production at Purdue and Oklahoma generally indicates a limitation in his wide receiver skill set, but if the weak parts of his game ever improve then he has the athleticism to become quite useful. Small as he is at 5-foot-10, 180 pounds,  Burks' athleticism is loud -- his 4.30-second 40-yard dash, 42.5-inch vertical jump and 131-inch broad jump are all well above the 90th percentile for wide receivers.
